items.transkript: Hello everyone. We are here for a new Rota program. Uh, hello Murat. How are you? >> Are you doing well too? >> I am doing well too. Thank you very much . Welcome. >> Today is Wednesday, November 25th. We are recording this program at 1 PM. Let's note that down first. >> Let's note it, yes. >> We had planned to talk about completely different things this week, but thank goodness both the world and Turkey gave us so much material that we changed the topics at the last minute. >> Unfortunately, that's what happened. >> Let's start somewhere. >> I mean, we would have liked to talk about projects that create value and our forward-looking dreams as much as possible, but they shattered our dreams . You know with what they shattered them . If you'd like, let's start with the fund for the first time. With the fund fraud . At the point we've reached, have the principal amounts, up to 1 million, been paid? We already know they haven't been paid. There are quite a few people complaining under the video, saying, " Hey brother, I received this much, I received 10%, I received 15%." >> Yes. I think, even if we say one or two of them are calculating wrong, so many people cannot be making a mistake just because they are writing about it. >> True. >> But let me repeat what we talked about at the very beginning, what I repeat every week. We would have liked to see the portfolios at the close of the 17th . The fact that this isn't shown already indicates that there is a huge problem here. I mean, it has never been disclosed to this day. "This was the portfolio on the 17th.""We sold these from the portfolio every week.""These remained.""These will be redeemed." Because it's impossible to sell a portion of private sector bonds. One must wait for their redemption. That is natural. There may be some positions, eurobonds, etc. Their maturity is waited for. Maybe a portion of the shares will be sold later, etc. First of all, no information is being given regarding this. Two, let's say there must be a date, like the beginning of 2024 for this fund. We have no information on how many people entered and how many left. How many received their money in full, how many were left inside? I mean, simply, in general, how much principal did those currently inside have? How many days on average had they stayed? This is also missing. >> There is a statement made by Mr. Cevdet Yılmaz. That statement is also completely, look at it however you like , like a picture taken from space. "81% of the investors in the fund received their money." How much of it did they receive? Who received how much? Which, from where did they receive it? From which fund did they receive it? It is not clear at all. >> I mean, we are deriving some math. Of course, we would also like to see this on a fund basis. We want to learn where it went. >> How much was paid to institutions, how much was paid to individuals. >> Yes. This fund business, I mean, there is no need to say how this should be done. It is clear how it should be done . It seems the management has such an intention. However, this, of course, shows how big and complex this fund business is. Their insistence on this matter, that is, their insistence on not disclosing this, and a piece of news constantly pops up. A few news items pop up. News comes out saying the principal in the funds is such and such amount. So, it comes out as a list of 108 people from these individuals. And our curiosity... >> Don't even get into those parts, because there are people in between who have nothing to do with the funds. There are completely different, entirely separate structures there as well. >> It's not related to just 108 people. Another piece of information was given that it involves slightly under 200 companies and a few hundred people. Therefore, there is a lot of information , but it is not information we can actually use. Since this isn't usable information, it inevitably creates speculation throughout the market. We wrote about things that weren't done at all. Perhaps some things were actually done quite well. We don't know about those either. They go to waste in the meantime, by the way. Because we don't know what happened. I mean, we don't even know what was done in which fund. We have a problem like that. The fund business is growing even larger than we estimated. Let’s see what it brings, but this is a massive problem in itself. The fact that this issue persists for so long, remains unresolved, and lacks details is a problem on its own. We have to say this. We need to say this . Therefore, the large number of people who have money in the fund and are concerned with this issue—and let me call it intensity rather than complaint —reveals the gravity of the situation. >> True. Do you know quantum physics? >> I know the name. I’ve never been involved with it. >> I am a bit curious about this subject. Like, especially regarding how computers , quantum computers function, I read books about it with a bit of an amateur spirit. Turkey is like a country that puts quantum physics into practice almost exactly. Funds were paid and not paid at the same time. I mean, this is what quantum physics is. A subatomic particle can be here in the same place at the same time, or it can be 10,000 km away somewhere in space. It shows very sudden leaps. While digital operations are between 1 and 0, in quantum computers, it can be anything between 1 and 0. It cannot be 1 or 0. Let me explain it with a general description, like it can be anywhere. It's actually a very deep subject. Like the lion issue we had, for example. I mean, was it in Istanbul or not? Like Schrödinger's cat. We even invented Schrödinger's lion. Was it seen or not? Were payments made in the funds or not? How much was paid? I think they will probably try to explain something this complex and non-transparent with quantum physics or something. That’s the joke of it, but it has gone beyond the joke. There is genuinely a serious reaction in society regarding this. I constantly want to break this down into layers. Meaning, the first layer is political, the second is bureaucratic, the third is those involved in the operation, and the fourth layer is the citizens who invested in the funds, suffered losses, and are crushed under all of this. As long as this hasn't been explained since the past, since the public offerings made starting from 2021, the biggest problem, the crisis of confidence in Turkey, will continue to grow. That’s what I see. The biggest impact of this is the recent melting we’ve experienced in Central Bank reserves. Let’s come to that subject. We will discuss the fund crisis in depth politically. You know it was a list of 108 people just a moment ago. There are also people on that list of 108 who have absolutely nothing to do with funds. In fact, there are people who have nothing to do with finance, who bought securities some time ago, held them for a while, sold them after the price went up significantly, and ended up on that list simply because they made over 100 million in profit. So, I frankly have huge question marks in my mind about how a system, a law, or a regulation is applied here, or if it is applied at all. That is why I see that the loss of confidence is becoming more of an issue every day; for this reason, not only due to legal problems but also because of this money traffic from the past, some foreign funds are no longer investing in Turkish assets, even in dollar-denominated ones—which we will also discuss regarding Eurobonds—and are fleeing. Let me give you a statistic. Between September 16 and November 23, 44.5 billion dollars left the Central Bank reserves, including the impact of the decline in gold prices. In the 10-day period between November 13 and November 23 alone, 21.9 billion dollars left. When we look at the reserves excluding swaps, the point we have reached right now is 1.9 billion. It looks like that will probably turn negative today as well. Because the price of gold has come down. We will have another reserve loss from that as well. The wealth effect of this, the effect on consumption—companies are currently in a very major problem. Many companies are struggling to restructure their debts, filing for bankruptcy or concordat; at the same time, unpaid credit cards and consumer loans—we will provide all of these with specific numbers and levels, and we will also present them by running forward-looking simulations. What do you say about the reserves? Will they come back? >> Now, let me step back a little bit on this subject. First of all, we are experiencing a significant change all over the world. With the Iran War, the rise in oil prices triggered many things . This, of course, has to do with inflation, but interest rates are going up globally. Therefore, we are a country that runs a financing deficit. We need external financing, and we are a country that needs to re-borrow by increasing the amount as the maturity of existing open financing comes due. Therefore, our costs are going up in the first place. So, there is a reason here for foreign positions to be closed. Interest rates are going up all over the world. Stock markets are coming down. If investment alternatives in the world are more attractive than those in Turkey , or even close to them, a foreigner who has invested in Turkey packs their bags and leaves. You don't take risks like this. You don't take currency risk here. Why would I invest in a currency that is losing around 20%annually when the world is smart? >> We, of course, during this whole period , were actually trying to bring our program—this inflation reduction program —to a point, especially in the year before the election, that is, in 2027, to reach a certain level significantly. First of all, we could not reach this point. Every year, if not two, at least one major event happens to us, and that major event jolts us, disrupts the balances, and delays what we want to do . >> Unfortunately, most of those major events come from the political side. >> Of course, I am talking about the ones inside the country. Geopolitical events. >> Okay, there is nothing we can do, but that’s where it has reached. Naturally, the fund came on top of this. Along with the fund, one of the important issues is that foreigners, locals, everyone, as we discussed before , their first reaction is to move to liquidity and park in the short term. Of course, moving to liquidity and parking in the short term has two types of consequences. One, if there is a good return in the long term, they give that up. When it comes to the short term, they say the return here is very low. They say it is not worth it here. Therefore, they also review their investment decisions once again. While all this is happening, we see that the market has started to deteriorate. For instance, as we will explain now, the credit market has deteriorated. So what are we going to do when the credit market deteriorates? The Central Bank eases the limits it applies to loans a little bit. It says, uh, we were growing loans by 4.5%, grow them by 5%, we were growing by 2%, grow them by 2.5%, etc., and we completely left SME loans alone. It makes a lot of decisions there. We are increasing the loans. Because pressure is coming from two things. One , we think loans should grow faster, and at the same time, we need to cut interest rates. I mean, by doing both, otherwise we have accelerated a lot in loans, especially non-performing loans, in the last 3-4 months. Let's talk about the numbers now. When all this happens, of course, we are heading somewhere like this. The world is raising interest rates. All returns in the world have gone upwards. On top of normal treasury bonds, the interest rates paid by the private sector have gone upwards. >> Spreads have increased. >> Spreads have increased. And investment options have diversified significantly. And as I said, foreigners in Turkey are packing their bags and leaving. This is the natural result of the market. I mean , there is no need to do anything. But we are in a market where we have to react in the exact opposite way to what they expect. >> Yes. And on the other hand, we were talking about an interest rate cut, I mean, just imagine. 100 basis points on December 10th, everyone, all economists are now saying they will cut. >> However, the last thing I will say here is this. There is a very dramatic difference between what we talked about 3-3.5 years ago regarding the Central Bank's foreign exchange position and today. What is that? Before the elections prior to this one, the Central Bank balance sheet was roughly like this. 140 billion dollars in KKM open position . On top of that, 70 billion dollars in open open position. >> Yes. >> So we were in an open position of 210 billion dollars. Where are we today compared to that 210 billion dollars? We are at zero. By the way, 210 billion dollars passed to the private sector as an open position. A very large portion passed to the private sector in terms of open position. Therefore, compared to the past, there is a trend deterioration , but this trend deterioration, for example, compared to the position we were in before the previous elections, is not something to be compared to that , I mean, we are not in such places or even close to that. We are not at such a point either. Therefore, we are talking about a trend deterioration. Regarding this, the Central Bank Governor gave information to Anadolu Agency. He implied that there is no change in their policies and that a regulation regarding withholding tax could be made in harmony with the treasury. It must be emphasized at that very point that in the regulation to be made regarding withholding tax, guys, they are not currently turning to foreign currency anyway. If you lowered the 17.5 %withholding tax to 10%right now, who would exchange foreign currency and come back? A very large portion is already underwater. You know, in our culture, we tend to have a "Catholic marriage" with losing positions until they turn a profit. That's why we have to wait a bit, but on the other hand, we need to see if the decision on the 10%withholding tax for institutions will be reversed in such a short time. I don't think it can be reversed easily . Did you look at the latest figure? It's around 1.8, I think, maybe 1.7% monthly devaluation. You were saying 1.9 . I'm calculating it as 1.9 in the current trend. >> Let's call it 1.8. >> Okay. With a 1.8 return on 36, netting it out with 10%...at the rate institutions are borrowing today, adding 300 basis points on top of 4%—which we know they are borrowing at much higher rates, like 7% —do you know what the annualized amount left in their pockets in dollar terms is ? 2.2%. That's why they are leaving. I mean, that's why they aren't staying here. Well, what about the 200 basis points—I mean, I’m coming to Turkey—on top of that 400 basis points where they tell you to go to Turkey for capital and pay an extra 200 basis points for the risk premium, which brings it to 3.2, 3.5. Frankly, while taking on Turkey's risk is very short-term, we have some Eurobonds right now paying 6.5%. When you go to slightly longer maturities, like 1 year 9 months, 1 year 8 months, they pay 10.5%. Add another 8 months on top, and we have Eurobonds paying 12%. So, do you think they will go from here ? I mean, would they take such a risk? You said they wouldn't. Well, we started talking about this a few weeks ago regarding foreigners. It has become very limited for foreigners to stay in the Turkish Lira and generate returns by taking short-term positions. I mean, they are playing for very low returns compared to before. Two, especially November is the month for closing positions abroad. If everyone has made their money for the year... >> it's Thanksgiving today, after all. >> Therefore, there is also a closing effect coming from there. Of course, how does the impact come in the meantime? Let's look at a few levels. One of the levels is, just as you said, foreigners are reducing their positions . Two, individuals are not buying foreign currency for now. We aren't seeing anything like that. There is no such trend. They are buying, but the amounts are small. >> Institutions are generally closing out right now. >> Let's move on to institutions. Now, I want to provide some information . Because I think this is important, especially regarding loans. In Turkey, the total of individual and commercial loans for Turkey-based entities—not loans given to foreigners, but to Turkey residents—is 28.3 trillion TL. Let me express this as a percentage . 7.1 trillion, which is 25%, are loans given to individuals. 25%are loans given to SMEs. The sum of these already makes 50%. Total commercial loans are 72.5%. I especially want to mention the foreign currency side of this. 32%of total loans, but 44%of commercial loans are in foreign currency. For a period, to limit the growth rate of foreign currency loans, the Central Bank heavily restricted their monthly increases, or those over 2 months, 8 weeks. >> Down to 1 percent levels. >> Even to halves, my friends. It had pulled them down significantly. >> On a monthly basis, yes. >> As the exchange rate also moved slowly, their share in total commercial loans was slightly above 50. It came down to 44. Because they are also buying on one hand. Therefore, we should also look at what we call carry trade from this perspective. So, what were companies looking at when using foreign currency loans? At the exchange rate growth speed and the cost of TL loans. They would say, if there is a reasonable difference between the two, let me go and use a foreign currency loan. Especially after news of decreasing Central Bank reserves, the fact that the exchange rate reached a monthly growth speed of around 1.80-1.90, that is nearly 2, let me open a parenthesis here regarding the foreign currency positions of some companies. The Central Bank also allowed a slight increase in loans. It allows for a certain amount of loan growth almost every month. It is increasing the growth rate a bit more. Inevitably, some companies will emerge saying, "I should close this foreign currency position a little bit." It seems we are seeing quite high demand from companies in the last week's slight increase, but companies sometimes enter a few billion and drop a few billion. That depends on other reasons. >> It was tax payments. >> Tax payments, loan payments, and so on. >> Salary payments and the like. >> We may see something like that again here, but it feels like companies have stopped these increases in foreign currency loans and might even want to close some positions when they hear this news. There is nothing with individuals yet. The main thing we need to pay attention to domestically is individuals; we will see the data from last week, the week we saw movement on the individual side, tomorrow. But there was nothing before that. That is the place that needs to be watched closely. But at least I talked to banks , I talked to the market, and so on. I don't expect any significant movement in individuals as of last week, but the data needs to come in. I mean, this isn't something that happens just by me talking to three or five banks individually. But at least, I am a bit comfortable there. Nothing appears to be there. But the exchange rate side seems like it will be a bit troublesome. How will the Central Bank succeed in maintaining this balance? We would like to see that. I mean, it looks like a bit of a difficult operation. Especially in the second week of December, if I'm not mistaken, either on the ninth or the tenth. >> On the tenth. >> On the tenth, the Central Bank will hold a meeting regarding the interest rate decision. There isn't much time left until then. Two weeks remain. Let's see what kind of decision they will make. What do you think? Both regarding the exchange rate developments and the Central Bank's decision. >> Now, regarding the exchange rate, I more or less understand the Central Bank's recent monthly accelerations. The reason is, I guess, that it is being done to at least support the exporter profile, which needs to compete with other countries, against the rise in input costs—even if used for some exports— such as raw materials and semi-finished goods, which are petrol and its derivatives, due to this geopolitical situation. But the Central Bank's job is quite difficult in the period ahead. The decision to be made in December is a catch-22 situation, with no easy way out . The reason for this is primarily the domestic wealth loss, as the fund crisis and the drop in gold prices point to a loss exceeding five trillion. Since this will put significant pressure on the expenditure side through consumers, we know how corporate production volumes have fallen, where the Sameks index has bottomed out, and that the ISO index has been low for nearly 30 months now. Within this framework, we know that the loans taken are not for investment but at least to keep the business running, to pay interest, and to cover certain expenses. Meanwhile, there are also loans that cannot be repaid and have turned into non-performing loans, and we clearly see these accelerating recently. It is a system that feeds itself. Like a row of dominoes. Today, it doesn't seem to be present in SMEs or large enterprises, but frankly, I don't trust certain figures there very much. We need to take a closer look at the non-performing loans. In fact, nearly 200 billion had been added to what we call second-degree loans—those with the potential to turn into non-performing loans—from June to that period. It had been added up until September. I believe it has increased even further from September to this period on the non-performing loan side. It is unfortunately becoming a system that feeds itself in a negative sense. When businesses fall into this state regarding non-performing loans, layoffs increase. We constantly hear about layoffs in Bursa, industrial zones, Denizli, Gaziantep, Kayseri, and everywhere else ; there are significant layoffs and pullbacks in the manufacturing industry . I do not think the general framework on the exchange rate side can be easily pulled downward while the global conjuncture continues like this in the upcoming period. The Central Bank will likely abandon inflation in 2027. I have become firmly convinced that the elections will not be held in 2028. In fact, the possibility of them occurring in the first six months of 2027 has started to seem extremely strong to me. As long as these signals keep coming, I don't think the interest rate side will be sufficient to provide financial stability, even at these levels, in terms of managing expectations amid such serious spikes in the exchange rate. However, I also think that such high interest rates on business, commercial, and SME loans bringing companies to this state could also significantly increase non-performing loans, not only within these credit lines but also in personal loans. I mean, there is a study I have conducted. If you like, I can summarize it briefly. That study is as follows. If the fund crisis eliminates 10%of wealth or has negatively impacted wealth by 10%, which the calculations more or less point to. I find it to be around 13 %. A figure around 5 trillion. Due to the sum of gold and the drop in gold prices plus the fund crisis. >> The total. >> While the current non-performing loan ratio for personal loans is 7.2%, in the simulation—this is not a guess, it's a simulation—it rises to 9.3%by the end of next May. It's like the chicken or the egg dilemma , where rising unemployment—caused by SMEs entering payment crises—is pushing the current non-performing loan ratio of around 4.5%up toward 6%. In short, let's say this. On our path to balance and stabilize the economy, unfortunately, after maintaining financial stability for a while, we are now on the verge of losing it due to various accidents—global ones , internal political ones, and others that may arise. Therefore, I don't think the Central Bank's reserves can easily hold out, and I anticipate that institutions will continue to make some purchases in the coming period to close their open positions. I must say, I wouldn't want to be in the shoes of the Central Bank Governor, Mr. Kavcıoğlu. In that case, let me continue from where I left off and tie it together. As I said, in Turkey, a little over 70% of total loans are those extended to our companies. The sum of both their TL and foreign currency components is 20.5 trillion. 9 trillion of that is in foreign currency . 9 trillion roughly amounts to around 180 billion dollars. Some companies may want to close this. We will see. There seems to be an increase of 5 billion in the figures from last week regarding companies. But this is a figure that sometimes fluctuates every two weeks. Therefore, it may have reversed just this past week. We might encounter a different position . But, how much foreign currency can these companies really buy? Can they just come and buy foreign currency like crazy? They cannot. Even in the worst of times, only a portion of the foreign currency loans could be closed. You need to find TL for that. It is not an easy life. Besides, it doesn't serve the interests of some, like exporters and so on. Therefore, I do not expect any massive, intense closing of foreign currency loans or any strange positioning on the corporate side in the near future. >> There might not be a loan there, because we also know what some companies are doing. >> Oh, absolutely, absolutely. Well, the exact figure isn't clear, but we estimate it to be between 15 and 20 billion dollars. Perhaps part of that 5 billion closed figure comes from there. I don't know that. We aren't saying anything for sure. It is very difficult to say. But as I said before, I mentioned it to highlight the figure here. I do not expect an election in 2027. My opinion on this could change very quickly, of course, but as of now—and I have felt this way for a long time—I do not expect such a thing. In the current climate, I wouldn't attempt such an election. Well, what if this happened—let me ask you a question . If signals of a major crisis in the first six months of 2027 become very strong, wouldn't the government want to do it then? Because once that crisis hits, there won't be any time left to recover for 2028. >> True, but for that decision to work, only they would need to know, and no one else could know. >> Very true. I think someone would leak it . >> Let me summarize it from here. Our loan quality is deteriorating rapidly. So, the non-performing loan ratio is rising , and we've taken a measure to solve this by enabling more lending. Let's provide more credit. Therefore, the economic management thinks that a portion of the non-performing loans will decrease this way. At the same time, the Central Bank is cutting interest rates, but due to export pressures or other reasons, it is also pushing the exchange rate slightly upward. The spread between them has narrowed significantly. A series of decisions will need to be made here. For instance, should we lower the exchange rate pace to 1.5, at the latest by January? Should we raise interest rates or lower them? Or should we increase the credit growth rate further; a series of decisions like these will need to be made. Some of these decisions might negatively affect others. For example, let’s provide more TL loans, but the gap between the interest rate and the exchange rate has narrowed considerably . If the market says, "I'll switch to foreign currency," for instance, this will have a negative impact. >> Indeed. >> Currently, if it continues at this pace , the year-end exchange rate is heading toward around 51.80. >> Yes. >> I wanted to point that out from here. We aren't saying it will definitely go just under 52 if it continues like this. It looks like it will close somewhere around there if it proceeds, but it seems we will now be talking every week about the credit side, which we didn't pay much attention to 3 months ago and only discussed generally once a month. >> Exactly that. >> And funds were added on top of it. Let's also take a look at the international scene, if you’d like. There is a series of developments abroad as well. Now, with the Fed going to raise rates and so on, there are developments there too. Also, that company we all know as Cloud has made its IPO. At the same time, there is a tremendous amount of AI debt, and those AI debts have gone to interesting places. The spreads on American bonds have begun to widen significantly. There are developments like that over there, too. What do you say about this new IPO and the borrowings? >> Actually, let me put it this way. We were driving, connected to GPS, enjoying our coffee, and suddenly we were awakened by that cold digital voice saying, "You have gone off-route." The thing taking us off-route isn't just interest rates. As you were saying earlier, that interest rates have gone up. Interest rates go up, then down, then up, then down. Especially the long-term ones. I mean, in the last month, we’ve seen the American 10-year yields hit 5.15, go down to 4.80, climb back from 4.80 to 5.10 s and 5.15 s, and as of today, return to 4.86. So, there is a significant amount of volatility there. That’s how I see it. Real pension funds or investment funds, long-term thinking investment funds, have pulled back a bit here at the moment. To see some stabilization in the short term. The real trigger was; as of last week, or the week before when we started discussing it, the debates surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese woman, whether she was an agent, and whether the goods or chips going to China were illegal. Following that, a decision came from the board of directors. They removed him from the CEO position. Over the past week, there was some sort of internal appointment, let's say, but while people were discussing how that wouldn't be enough, the American government suddenly intervened in Nvidia and brought him back. They brought him to the head of the board. They put him in charge of the board of directors. And they re-equipped him with authority . But the way I see it, let's think about it this way. I'll explain at length, but to get the full picture clear, especially chip companies and AI companies are reporting incredible balance sheets. For example, in the balance sheet announced yesterday, Dell showed 60 billion in revenue and incredible earnings. There is a massive amount in terms of cash. We are building a skyscraper right now. We don't even have an idea yet of where this skyscraper is heading. Everyone is staring up at it, and suddenly Jensen Huang's thing comes out . Then the American government says, "I'm going to hold an inquiry here." The dates of December 1-3, for instance, are very critical regarding this matter. Following that, the SEC makes a statement. It says, "I will go and check this construction to see if there are any cracks." Then we see all the hedge funds, because of the interest rate hikes you mentioned , acting like a choir, saying, "Oh no, there's a cash gap here." "Their free cash flows won't be positive ." "They will have to borrow money here." And because of that, saying "let's sell these," there is incredible volatility. Stocks that have risen 13-15%in a day come back down by 10-11%or 7%the next day. What I see is actually this. Hedge fund anarchism. Let's put it that way. While leverage positions were up to 75%in July , the point we have reached today is this EPAR data. It is taken from a Goldman Sachs report . I should mention that too. It reached the lowest point. It hit 42% . I mean, everyone is speaking based on their own positions. No one is speaking with a long-term investment perspective. What they are saying is, "steal the minaret and find a cover for it." Within that framework, conversations around AI , which has profitability, will continue , and will cause significant debates along with the pains of technological change over the next 3 years, are unfortunately dragging us into very short-term fluctuations and, consequently, interest rate debates. The main framework, as far as I can see , is where we will evolve in commodity and energy prices due to geopolitical developments abroad. Despite all the ships hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, despite missile attacks, and despite the Houthis hitting skyscrapers in Saudi Arabia; the signal given to me by oil, which drops to $ 87 , then rises to $ 91, and then drops back to $ 89, keeps the probability of a recession or stagflation in the American economy from the mid-2027 onwards very much on the agenda. Accordingly, I think the American Central Bank, the Fed, will start discussing interest rate cuts again from September. One more thing, one more perspective should be added to this. The personal consumption index to be released today will be very important. The volatility these will create will be at an extreme level. However, given how stressful housing sales are in the upcoming period, the fact that they are declining, and mortgage rates being at peak levels, we need to step back in the short term and adjust ourselves accordingly, even though the American economy currently shows vitality. Both as a country and as companies. In short, it seems we have fallen right into the middle of a perfect storm. I think the most logical approach in a perfect storm is to adopt a more moderate course of action rather than trying to ride the waves. >> I agree. >> Let me add this. The fact that, especially developed countries, including emerging ones, are resorting to net borrowing well beyond their growth rates puts tremendous pressure on interest rates. Even though they try to regulate this periodically by changing maturities, borrowing short-term, or announcing some buybacks—like in America—the pressure on interest rates continues. On top of that, these AI investments, including data centers, are coming into the private sector at a much higher rate than the trend to date. When I say including data centers, most of it is related to data centers. Costs here, borrowing costs, are moving up rapidly, and long-term borrowing is becoming difficult. >> They weren't borrowing anyway. For instance, I know about CoreView; when bond yields started hitting 16%, they started shifting their borrowing entirely to the short term, saying they wouldn't borrow long-term. >> Yes. And this also puts pressure on interest rates. This puts immense pressure on all other investment products and investments in general. Because when someone starts borrowing at 8%returns for 10, 20, or 30 years, the first question becomes: What can I invest in to earn more than 8 or 10 percent annually in dollar terms? That is exactly where the crunch point lies. Therefore, there is tremendous interest rate pressure on all types of investment products. We would be wrong to think like this about the near future: If the Fed, the European Central Bank, or central banks cut short-term rates, then the problem will be solved. All interest rates will fall. It doesn't work like that. It works exactly the opposite. That's the whole point. >> Now, I will add one more thing there. There is a very interesting point. An indicator, actually. 2-year inflation swaps are currently around 2.65. The fact that 2-year inflation swaps are at 2.65 means that, in real terms, I will essentially be earning a return of around 2.65 in the period ahead. When you have a 2.65 real return in dollar-denominated interest, and a maturity premium is added on top of that for ten-year bonds, bringing it to around 4.80 or 5, we see that it equalizes with what we call the equity risk premium. In that case, the investor naturally says, "Instead of doing this, I'd rather go and take a position in bonds." The takeaway from this for us, or what it points to, is that as long as there is a 2.65 risk premium in America and we offer 2.2-2.3%annually in Turkish Lira to investors coming here, it means the Turkish Lira has no appeal. We seem to be fixated on interest rates , but there are many structural things that need to be done here. That seems to be the case. Let's pause here if you'd like. >> Yes. >> This week This week, I would like to introduce a book by one of my former bosses and chairmen of the board, Tevfik Altınok. Tevfik Altınok worked at the Ministry of Finance in Ankara and led the Treasury. >> One of the legendary bureaucrats. >> Yes. My first meeting with Mr. Tevfik was in 1985, if I'm not mistaken. I had just graduated from university. I went for a job interview at the Koç Group. Mr. Tevfik said, "Look, in Turkey, things are generally not like this; we usually just have an accounting department." In fact, in most companies, the accounting department often handles human resources as well. That’s not the case for us. He had started working at Koç Holding. He said, "We are establishing a finance department.""We will hire young friends who have just graduated from university here," he said. At that time, I needed to go abroad for a short period. I went abroad. I didn't start there. Upon my return, I became a banker. After becoming a banker, I changed two banks for a while. My third bank was Koç Bank . When I arrived, Mr. Tevfik was the chairman of the board. >> That's right. >> And at Koç Holding, the entire finance department reported to him. Including the bank. We worked together for many years. Then he left Koç. For a period during the 2001 crisis, he went to manage all public banks and so on. Naturally, I have a personal history with Mr. Tevfik. Therefore, the book covers many details , and I am actually a part of some of the things he narrates. Because it talks about Koç Bank, the Koç Group, and the dynamics in the public and private sectors. It describes how they diverged on both sides. One of the important topics is how it shows the relationships between bureaucrats and politicians during that period, and even how powerful bureaucrats were on certain issues. He tells that too. It is an extremely interesting book called "Hazinedarbaşı" for understanding a period and better analyzing the differences with today. >> Let's show the screen, if you like. >> Therefore >> But it's not an old book. >> No, it’s a few months old. It’s a book that was released toward the middle of this year. So, it's a new book. I mean, it's not an old book. Let’s wish everyone a good week. >> Have a good week. Thank you.

items.transkript:
Hikmet Abi

Tahliye etmek değil, etmemek adaletsiz

Hani eleştiri bir haktı

Hikmet Çetin’i kaybettik.

Genç kuşakların tanıma şansına erişemediği müthiş bir “devlet” adamı idi.

Diyarbakır’dan, Lice’den çıkmış, Mekteb-i Mülkiye’yi bitirmiş, ABD’de kalkınma ekonomisi üzerine yüksek lisans yapmış, ardından Stanford Üniversitesi’nde planlama üzerine eğitim görmüş bir isimdi.

Daha sonra Devlet Planlama Teşkilatı’nda üst düzey görevlerde bulundu. İktisadi Planlama Daire Başkanlığı yaptı.

Ardından siyasete girdi. 12 Eylül öncesi Ecevit hükümetlerinde yer aldı. Darbe sonrası dönemde CHP olmadığı için Sosyal Demokrat Halkçı Parti çatısı altında kalsa da CHP’den ve sosyal demokrasiden ayrılmadı. Öz CHP’liydi ve kayyum Kılıçdaroğlu gelinceye kadar hep CHP’li kaldı. Parti içinde Baykal’a karşı bayrak açan zannederim ilk isimdi.

Siyasi kariyeri boyunca devlet bakanlığı, başbakan yardımcılığı, dışişleri başkanlığı, Meclis başkanlığı yaptı. En ilginci, “atanmış devlet başkanlığı” gibi bir görev de üstlendi.

ABD işgali sonrası Afganistan’ın normale dönmesi sürecinde NATO tarafından Afganistan’ı yönetmekle görevlendirildi. Kıdemli Sivil Temsilci sıfatıyla, Karzai ile birlikte Afganistan’ı yönetti. Daha doğrusu Karzai’ye ağabeylik yaparak yönetmeyi öğretti desem yeridir.

CHP’liydi ama tüm partilerin sempatisine sahipti. Süleyman Demirel’in en sevdiği ve en saygı duyduğu siyasetçilerin başında gelirdi. “Keşke CHP’de Hikmet Çetin gibi 10 adam daha olsa” dediğini bizzat duymuştum.

Benim için ise özel bir öneme sahipti.

DPT kökenli siyasetçiler benim için önemlidir ama Hikmet Çetin daha da önemliydi.

Bilirsiniz, siyasetçi taifesi ile aramda hep bir mesafe vardır.

Hikmet Çetin, arama mesafe koyma gereği duymadığım ve “Abi” diye hitap ettiğim tek siyasetçi oldu.

1980’lerden bu yana gelen tanışıklığımız ve dostluğumuzda eleştirilerim karşısında asla tepki göstermezdi. Arar ve nedenini sorardı, tartışırdık. Adına leke düşürecek hiçbir işin içinde olmadı. Zengin olmaktansa saygın olmayı tercih etti.

Cezaevinde olduğum süreçte ayakta zor duran hali ile dört kez ziyaretime geldi. Her hafta en az bir kez eşimi arayıp bir ihtiyacı olup olmadığını sordu. Özgür Özel’in mitinglerinde hep yanında, otobüsün üzerinde idi. Cezaevinde Özgür Özel’e “Miting boyunca Hikmet Abi ayakta kalıyor ve yoruluyor, ona bir sandalye verin lütfen” dedim.

Bir sonraki ziyaretinde “Niye benim yaşlı olduğum dedikodusunu yapıyorsun” diye geldi gülerek.

Bir başka ziyaretinde biz sohbet ederken odaya infaz koruma memuru arkadaşlar geldi ve “Üzerinizde kulaklık kalmış. Onu almamız lazım. İçeri sokamıyoruz onları” dediler kibarca.

Güldü, “Kulaklığım olmadan Fatih’le nasıl sohbet edeceğim” dedi.

Aylardır hastanede idi.

Ve kaybettik.

Geride yüzlerce neşeli, keyifli anı kaldı.

Çok kişi belki farkında değil.

Ama Türkiye çok önemli bir değerini daha kaybetti.

İlber, Hikmet Abi.

Onları özleyeceğiz. Benzerleri olmadığı için de çok ama çok arayacağız.

## Tahliye etmek değil, etmemek adaletsiz

Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya önceki gün tahliye edildi.

Fon vurgununun tek sorumlusu değildi, baş sorumlusu da değildi ve hatta en büyük vurguncu da değildi belki ama fon vurgununun simgesel ismiydi ve “ucu kime dokunursa dokunsun” ifadesinin inandırıcı görünmesinin tek ama tek göstergesiydi.

Ne yalan söyleyeyim, tutuklanmasını bile beklemiyordum ama tutuklandı.

19 günlük tutukluluktan sonra “sağlık gerekçeleri” ile tahliye edildi.

Bu söyleyeceklerim belki bazılarınızı kızdıracaktır ama ben Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’nın tahliye edilmesine tepki göstermiyorum.

Kaçma, kayıplara karışma, suç delillerini ortadan kaldırma tehlikesi olmadığına göre tahliye edilmesi bence normal, hatta belki doğru hareket.

Asıl mesele Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’nın tahliye edilmesi değil, başkalarının tahliye edilmiyor olması.

Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya sağlık gerekçeleri ile tahliye edilmiş. Kendi sağlığı mı, çocuklarının psikolojik sağlığı mı bilmiyorum. Hangi sağlık sorunu var, onu da bilmiyoruz. Belli ki dosyaya bir rapor konulmuş ve tahliye gerçekleşmiş.

Peki Murat Çalık’ın çok daha ciddi, çok daha önemli sağlık sorunları yok mu!

Sağlığı son derece bozuk olduğu halde aylarca tutuklu kalan ve cezaevinden sağ çıkacağına dair pek çok kişinin kaygı duyduğu başka tutuklular yok mu!

Asıl mesele Fatma Betül Hanım’ın tahliyesi değil, diğerlerinin tahliye edilmemesi.

## Hani eleştiri bir haktı

İki gün önce Ümit Özlale’nin fon vurgunuyla ilgili olarak Yeni Parti adına konuşmasının hatalı olduğunu yazdım.

Bana göre Özlale’nin bu konuda birkaç handikabı vardı.

Daha önce yaptığı bir açıklama tam olarak doğru çıkmamış, bu yüzden birkaç gazeteci sorun yaşamıştı. Bu da sonraki açıklamalarına en muhalif gazetecilerin bile mesafeli yaklaşmasına neden oluyordu.

Üslubu, büyük ihtimalle öğretim üyeliğinden ve akademisyenliğinden gelen alışkanlıkla didaktikti ve canlı yayında bile halk üzerinde etki yaratmıyordu.

Ve eşi muhalif bir kanalda gazeteci idi.

Yazımda Özlale ile ilgili tek bir kötü söz yoktu. Sadece o işe uygun olmadığını söylüyordum.

Özlale ailesinden tepki görünce şaşırdım.

Kendisi bir ortak dostumuz vasıtası ile, eşi ise Teke Tek ekibi aracılığıyla.

Ümit Bey’e aracılık yapan ortak dostumuza “Kendisine karşı olumsuz hiçbir tavrım yok. Sadece bu işe uygun olmadığını düşünüyorum.” dedim. Ortak dostumuz da benimle aynı fikirdeydi zannederim.

Eşi Serap Belovacıklı Özlale ise “Ümit’in gece gündüz memleket için nasıl kelle koltukta çalıştığını görüyorum. Bunu da bununla ilgili bir yazıya teşvik etmek için yazmıyorum, aman eşi devreye girdi gibi bir durum da olsun istemem. Sadece herkes ‘Aman abi, bana dokunmayın’ derken elini taşın altına koyan birine fazla haksızlık yapıldığını düşünüyorum. İki aydır düzenli olarak tehdit alıp bu psikolojiyle mücadeleye devam ederken bize yakın olduğunu düşündüğümüz insanlardan gelen eleştiriler daha yıkıcı oluyor.” demiş.

Öncelikle şunu söyleyeyim. Beni doğrudan arayabilirler, öcü değilim, arayanları yemiyorum.

Yazımda Ümit Bey’in çalışmalarına yönelik en ufak bir eleştiri yok. Sadece bu konuda sözcülük yapmasını doğru bulmadığımı nedenleri ile açıklıyorum. Benimki bir fikir. Doğru bulurlar, bulmazlar. Kendi bilecekleri iş ama yapılan açıklamaların gündem olmaması bile benim haklı olduğumu düşündürebilir. Hakaret etmeden, kızmadan, öfkelenmeden yaptığım fikir beyanına en çok bir meslektaş olarak Serap Belovacıklı’nın anlayışla yaklaşmasını beklerdim.

Ümit Bey’in çalışmalarına saygı duyuyorum.

Basit bir benzetme yapayım. Mesela bizim burada da Emre çok ama çok çalışıyor. Ama önceki gün çektiğimiz otomobil testinde direksiyona ben oturdum, o değil. Yakında yayınlanacak o videoda onun benden çok emeği olacak, kesin. Ama otomobili kullanıp test etmek benim işim. Emre’nin benden çok çalışmış olması ve perde arkasındaki bütün hazırlıkları yapması direksiyona da onun oturmasını gerektirmiyor. Pistte iki tur atınca midesi bulandı. Bilmem, anlatabildim mi!

İktidarın eleştiriler karşısındaki tavrını eleştirenlerin, kendilerine yönelik eleştiri bile sayılmayacak cümlelere daha olumlu yaklaşmalarını beklerdim.

Şaşırdım ve üzüldüm.
